`budget-complete($m,x_m,Z_m$)`. The finite-dimensional least-squares minimizer

Let $a<b$, let $j\ge1$ be an integer, and let $f\in C^{2j+2}([a,b])$. For $N\ge1$ set $h=(b-a)/N$, $I=\int_a^b f$, and
$$c_r:=\frac{B_{2r}}{(2r)!}\bigl(f^{(2r-1)}(b)-f^{(2r-1)}(a)\bigr),\qquad 1\le r\le j+1,$$
using the Bernoulli numbers of [[def-na-bernoulli-polynomials]]. Then
$$T_N(f)=I+\sum_{r=1}^{j}c_rh^{2r}+\varepsilon_N,\qquad |\varepsilon_N|\le C_jh^{2j+2},$$
where the level-independent finite constant
$$C_j:=|c_{j+1}|+\frac{(b-a)M_{2j+2}}{(2j+2)!}\|f^{(2j+2)}\|_\infty,\qquad M_{2j+2}:=\max_{0\le u\le1}|B_{2j+2}(u)|,$$
does not depend on $N$. Thus the remainder bound is uniform over every set of dyadic levels.

For each integer $n\ge0$, define the Legendre polynomial
$$
P_n(x):=\frac{1}{2^n n!}\frac{d^n}{dx^n}(x^2-1)^n,
$$
with $n!$ as in [[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]] and repeated derivatives as in [[def-higher-derivatives-and-smoothness]]. Define the unweighted pairing of real polynomials by
$$
\langle p,q\rangle_L:=\int_{-1}^1p(x)q(x)\,dx,\qquad \|p\|_L^2:=\langle p,p\rangle_L.
$$
The integral is the ordinary integral of a continuous function. The normalization and all polynomial identities needed for the orthogonal Galerkin scale are proved in [[lem-legendre-weighted-derivative-orthogonality-and-norm]].

For a relation $A\subseteq E\times E$ and $\rho>0$, define its resolvent as
the inverse relation
$$J_{\rho A}:=(I+\rho A)^{-1},\qquad J_{\rho A}(y)=\{x\in E:y-x\in\rho A(x)\},$$
where $\rho A(x)=\{\rho a:a\in A(x)\}$. Its domain is the set of $y$ for
which this value set is nonempty. At this point it may be partial and
set-valued; full domain and single-valuedness are separate conclusions of
[[thm-maximal-monotone-resolvent-is-firmly-nonexpansive]].

the coefficient, Brownian, and initial-moment hypotheses of
[[thm-superlinear-sde-global-existence-and-moments]]. For each integer
$N\ge\max(1,\lceil T\rceil)$, put $h=T/N$ and define $Y_0,\ldots,Y_N$ by
[[alg-tamed-euler-superlinear-drift]]. Then for every finite $p\ge1$,
$$\sup_{N\ge\max(1,\lceil T\rceil)}\ \max_{0\le n\le N}\mathbb E|Y_n|^p<\infty.$$
The bound may depend on $p,T$, the coefficient constants, and the initial
moments, but not on $N$ or $n$.

For the LQR data of [[def-ctrl1-linear-lqr-control-problem]], let $\mathcal F$ be nonempty and convex and let $u\in\mathcal F$. Put $g(t)=B(t)^Tp(t)+R(t)u(t)$, with the adjoint from [[def-ctrl1-lqr-adjoint-equation]]. If $u$ minimizes $J$ on $\mathcal F$, then
$$\int_0^T g(t)^T(v(t)-u(t))\,dt\ge0\qquad(v\in\mathcal F).$$
Conversely, if this variational inequality holds at $u$, then $u$ is the unique minimizer on $\mathcal F$.

Let $\Lambda$ be finite, contain $0$, and let the real basis
$(\psi_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\Lambda}$ be as in
[[def-chaos-orthonormal-tensor-basis]]. For real $u\in L^2(\rho)$ set
$c_\alpha=\langle u,\psi_\alpha\rangle$ and
$P_\Lambda u=\sum_{\alpha\in\Lambda}c_\alpha\psi_\alpha$ as in
[[def-finite-chaos-orthogonal-projection]]. Then
$$\|u\|_{L^2(\rho)}^2=\sum_{\alpha\in\Lambda}c_\alpha^2+
\|u-P_\Lambda u\|_{L^2(\rho)}^2.$$
The residual is orthogonal to $\mathcal P_\Lambda$,
$\mathbb E[u]=c_0$, and
$$\operatorname{Var}(u)=\sum_{\alpha\in\Lambda\setminus\{0\}}c_\alpha^2+
\|u-P_\Lambda u\|_{L^2(\rho)}^2.$$
Here $\operatorname{Var}(u)=\mathbb E[(u-\mathbb E u)^2]$; no completeness of
the polynomial family is assumed.

Let $T>0$, $N\ge1$, $h=T/N$, and let $y(t)$ solve the additive IVP of [[def-additive-ode-and-partition]] on $[0,T]$. Assume the exact path, all numerical states, and every selected implicit branch remain in a common compact convex tube with positive margin in the state domain. Suppose the uniform hypotheses of [[thm-imex-euler-local-order-and-stability]] hold on this tube and use the exact-root IMEX Euler map with exact initial value $y_0=y(0)$. Then there is a constant $C_T$, independent of $h$ and the step index, such that
$$\max_{0\le n\le N}\|y_n-y(t_n)\|_2\le C_T h.$$
This is a fixed-time first-order result for the selected local branch; it makes no assertion about other implicit roots.

Let $\mu_t$ be a continuous solution on $[0,T]$ with initial mass $M_1$, and let $\nu_t^R$ be the retained measure of the finite sectional system initialized by retaining the projection $P_\Delta\mu_0$ on pivots at most $R$ and placing the projected tail mass $\int_{(R,\infty)}x\,P_\Delta\mu_0(dx)$ in its reported reservoir. Assume $R$ is a pivot endpoint and $\Delta\le1$. Then
$$d_{BL}(\nu_t^R,\mu_t)\le e^{C_Tt}\left[C_QT\Delta+\frac{\Delta}{2}M_0(\mu_t)+\frac{M_1}{R}+\frac{2K_*M_1^2t}{aR}\right],\qquad 0\le t\le T,$$
where $C_Q$ is from [[lem-fixed-pivot-coagulation-fragmentation-quadrature-error]], $C_T$ is a finite bounded-number stability constant, and the terms proportional to $\Delta$, $R^{-1}$ are respectively the grid and cutoff errors. The reservoir itself is diagnostic and does not recreate the omitted transition law.

Let $d\ge1$, let $f:[0,1]^d\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, and use a level
hierarchy as in [[def-smolyak-univariate-level-hierarchy]]. Suppose its tensor
rules satisfy $Q_L^{\otimes d}(f)\to I_d(f)$ and its detail family is absolutely
summable in the sense of [[def-smolyak-absolute-detail-summability]]. For every
finite downward-closed $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb N_0^d$ containing $0$,
$$|I_d(f)-Q_\Lambda(f)|\le\sum_{\ell\in\mathbb N_0^d\setminus\Lambda}|\delta_\ell(f)|.$$
In particular, the dyadic composite-Simpson hierarchy satisfies the convergence
hypothesis for continuous $f$ by
[[lem-smolyak-dyadic-tensor-simpson-convergence]], and for the mixed-derivative
class of [[lem-smolyak-mixed-simpson-detail-decay]] the same hierarchy also
satisfies absolute summability.

Assume the hypotheses and parameter ranges of
[[thm-trust-region-global-liminf-gradient]], and let $f_{inf}$ be a lower
bound for $f$. For each target $0<\varepsilon\le1$, run
[[alg-trust-region-method]] until its first iterate with
$\|\nabla f(x_k)\|_2\le\varepsilon$. Define
$$c_\delta:=\min\left\{\frac1{2M_B},
\frac{\theta_C(1-\eta_2)}{2(L+M_B)}\right\},\qquad
c_R:=\min\{\Delta_0,\gamma_{dec}\min\{c_\delta,\Delta_{max}\}\},$$
where a zero denominator means $+\infty$, and put
$$c_P:=\min\{c_R,1/M_B\},\qquad
c_S:=\tfrac12\eta_1\theta_Cc_P>0.$$
Then the number $N_s$ of accepted steps before reaching the target and the
number $N_u$ of rejected trials obey
$$N_s\le\frac{f(x_0)-f_{inf}}{c_S\varepsilon^2},$$
$$N_u\le\frac{\log(\Delta_0/r_\varepsilon)+N_s\log\gamma_{inc}}
{|\log\gamma_{dec}|},\qquad
r_\varepsilon:=\min\{\Delta_0,\gamma_{dec}\min\{c_\delta\varepsilon,
\Delta_{max}\}\}.$$
Here $\log$ denotes the natural logarithm of a positive real.
Consequently, accepted steps and total trials $N_s+N_u$ are
$O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. An outer cap at least
the resulting total-trial bound suffices for the finite-budget algorithm to
return `target-achieved` or `stationary`, with gradient norm at most
$\varepsilon$.
